item.title: Silicon qubits surpass 99.99% gate fidelity while operating three at once
item.description: Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform for building scalable quantum computers as they are compatible with the semiconductor manufacturing technologies used to produce today's computer chips. However, they have an important weakness: silicon spin qubits typically lose accuracy when several qubits are under parallel control. To be useful, quantum computers will need to operate many qubits simultaneously without compromising the accuracy of their operations. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Molecular snapshots reveal how viral enzymes switch between inserting and removing DNA
item.description: Bacteriophages, or viruses that infect bacteria, have a fiendishly simple purpose in life: attach to a bacterial cell, inject their DNA and then use the host's genetic machinery to reproduce. In doing so, they may have evolved some of the most efficient gene-editing tools ever seen in nature. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Single 2D crystal transforms into transistor with built-in insulation and electrical contacts
item.description: A transistor normally requires several fundamentally different materials—a semiconductor to carry current, an insulating dielectric to control it and metallic contacts through which current enters and leaves.
